scaleComparison.caption: Compare the raw Potential Scale (all available pitches in one octave) with a consonant Actual Scale, an invalid 7-note subset that breaks melodic consonance, and a 5-note Pentatonic scale.

scales.title: Potential Scale (Gām-e Bel-Qovveh — subset across C4–C5)
scales.description: Using every available microtonal step in one melodic line sounds cluttered and unmusical; this is a raw pitch inventory, not a playable piece scale.

scales.title: Valid Actual Scale (Gām-e Bel-Fe'l — Heptatonic)
scales.description: Selecting 7 consonant pitches (C, D, E, F, G, A, B♭, C) yields a cohesive actual scale structured as two dāngs plus a ṭanīnī.

scales.title: Invalid 7-Note Selection (Counterexample)
scales.description: An arbitrary 7-note pick (C, D-koron, E-koron, E♮, F, B) clashes with Persian melodic consonance norms and creates jarring microtonal clusters and gaps.

scales.title: Pentatonic Comparison (5-Note Scale)
scales.description: Common in East Asian, African, and Indigenous American traditions: five pitches per octave (C, D, E, G, A, C) with no semitones.

degreeHierarchy.caption: Same actual scale (C–D–E–F–G–A–B♭–C), different modal feelings: hear how shifting Shāhed (ش), Īst (ی), Khātemeh (خ), and a Moteghayyer (م) transforms the mode.

presets.label: Textbook Example: Shāhed = G, Khātemeh = D
presets.note: Exact textbook experiment (pp. 23–24): starting and dwelling on degree 5 (G, Shāhed ش), pausing briefly on F (Īst ی), and resolving definitively on degree 2 (D, Khātemeh خ).

presets.label: Shifted Gravity: Shāhed = E, Khātemeh = C
presets.note: Identical 7 pitches, completely different modal ethos: emphasizing E (ش) and resolving to C (خ) changes the affective center.

presets.label: Moteghayyer (م): B♮ ascending → B♭ descending
presets.note: Demonstrates a variable degree (Moteghayyer م): the 7th degree rises to B♮ (493.88 Hz) when pulled upward toward C5, then lowers to B♭ (466.16 Hz) in descent.

dastgahTree.caption: The 7 canonical Dastgāhs and 5 derived Āvāzes (12 modal branches) growing from the Radif.

dastgahs.name: Shūr
dastgahs.note: The largest branch of the Persian modal tree, giving rise to four of the five canonical Āvāzes (plus Bayāt-e Kord in some classifications).

dastgahs.name: Navā
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh with no canonical derived Āvāzes; its Darāmad II is a classic example of a single-Shāhed opening.

dastgahs.name: Segāh
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh featuring prominent modally specific gūshehs such as Zābol and Mokhālef.

dastgahs.name: Chahārgāh
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh sharing named modally specific gūsheh types such as Zābol, Mokhālef, and Ḥeṣār.

dastgahs.name: Homāyūn
dastgahs.note: Parent Dastgāh of the fifth canonical Āvāz, Bayāt-e Eṣfahān; also contains major gūshehs such as Shūshtarī.

dastgahs.name: Māhūr
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh known for extensive modulations through modally specific gūshehs like Delkash and Erāq, unified by the characteristic Māhūr forūd.

dastgahs.name: Rāst-Panjgāh
dastgahs.note: Independent Dastgāh whose Darāmad I illustrates a two-Shāhed hierarchy and traverses wide modal territory.
